blogs.title: Why Orthogonal Finetuning Matters: Preserving Knowledge in Large Models
blogs.description: An introduction to the concept of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT), explaining how orthogonal transformations keep the relational geometry of pretrained weights intact, why this leads to better generalization, and how it differs from popular methods like LoRA and adapters.

blogs.title: From Block‑Diagonal to Butterfly: Making Orthogonal Finetuning Parameter‑Efficient
blogs.description: A deep‑dive into the parameter‑efficiency problem of OFT, the limitations of block‑diagonal matrices, and how the butterfly factorization—borrowed from the Fast Fourier Transform—creates dense orthogonal matrices with only O(d log d) trainable parameters.

blogs.title: The Information Transmission View: Visualizing Sparse Orthogonal Matrix Factorizations
blogs.description: Explains the novel graph‑based “information transmission” perspective introduced in the paper, showing how multiplying sparse matrices can be seen as routing information across a grid, and why this viewpoint helps design efficient factorizations.

blogs.title: BOFT in Action: Adapting Vision Transformers, Language Models, and Diffusion Models
blogs.description: Summarizes the empirical results of Orthogonal Butterfly (BOFT) across different domains—vision, NLP, and text‑to‑image generation—highlighting performance gains over LoRA, adapters, and standard OFT while keeping parameter counts low.

blogs.title: The Maths Behind BOFT: Expressivity, Spectral Guarantees, and Inductive Bias
blogs.description: Breaks down the theoretical insights of the paper—expressivity compared to block‑diagonal OFT, preservation of spectral norms, connections to metric learning, and how butterfly structures introduce useful inductive biases for better generalization.
